title: Innovation Saturation Does Not Robustify Kalman-Filtered Importance Ratios in LLM Reinforcement Learning

contributions.purpose: Tests whether innovation saturation, a classical robust-filtering technique, can fix Kalman Policy Optimization's (KPO) sensitivity to the process-to-measurement noise ratio Q/V.
contributions.mechanism: Implements Innovation-Saturated KPO (IS-KPO), which clips the Kalman innovation when it exceeds a scale-aware threshold, and evaluates it against KPO under weak smoothing.
contributions.evaluation: On MATH-500, IS-KPO recovers only 6.6% of the 11.79 percentage-point performance gap between weak and strong smoothing, with the improvement not statistically significant (p ~= 0.16).
contributions.source_quote: We present the first empirical study of innovation saturation for LLM policy optimization, testing whether this classical robust filtering technique can address KPO's sensitivity to the Q/V ratio.

contributions.purpose: Identifies a fundamental design tension explaining why innovation saturation cannot help KPO.
contributions.mechanism: Shows that activating innovation clipping requires low measurement noise V, but low V increases the Kalman gain and undermines the smoothing KPO relies on for stability.
contributions.evaluation: Diagnostic analysis: with KPO's V = 1.0 the clipping threshold (~3.06) far exceeds actual innovation magnitudes (~0.5), so the saturation mechanism almost never activates (clip fraction < 1e-6).
contributions.source_quote: We identify a fundamental design tension: activating innovation clipping requires low measurement noise V, but low V increases the Kalman gain and undermines the smoothing that KPO relies on for stability.

contributions.purpose: Explains diagnostically why the saturation mechanism fails in KPO's operating regime.
contributions.mechanism: Analyzes innovation statistics, showing heavy tails exist but do not exceed the clipping threshold under KPO's operating regime.
contributions.evaluation: Innovation statistics analysis (clip fraction < 1e-6; threshold ~3.06 vs innovations ~0.5), ruling out parameter tuning as a resolution.
contributions.source_quote: We provide diagnostic analysis explaining why the mechanism fails, including innovation statistics showing that heavy tails exist but do not exceed the clipping threshold under KPO's operating regime.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We investigate whether innovation saturation, a well-established technique for robustifying Kalman filters against outliers (Fang et al., 2018), can reduce KPO's sensitivity to the Q/V ratio.
Our work tests whether this robustification transfers to LLM policy optimization, finding that the structural requirements for activation conflict with the smoothing requirements of KPO.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper (declared in the title and abstract): innovation saturation recovers only 6.6% of the performance gap, not statistically significant (p ~= 0.16), and the paper rules it out as a robustification strategy. All contributions are findings/analysis; no new performing method is claimed.
